# P37.57b — Whole-graph TI-6/TI-7 audits over a real spine (R11-DEBT-01b)

- **Spec:** `docs/tickets/485_P37.57b__whole-graph-audits.md`
  (manifest row 485; `R11-DEBT-01`, split `b` of `P37.57` — S4c context-ceiling split)
- **Base:** `r11/P37.57a-projection-rebuild-ci` (`2e6a8796`)
- **Config:** `implement-spec … live_verification=false` — engineering dispatch.
  Gate `none`; not OM-20; no live legs; no production mutations.

## What this changes

ADR-025 made TI-1..TI-8 pipeline data-quality checks over the batch a writer is
about to assert — and recorded the gap this row closes: *TI-6/TI-7 are batch
checks, so they see only the batch handed to them; a full-graph audit remains a
separate nightly job.* `db.graph_audit` is that job, and
`sig-db graph-audit --dsn …` is its command — **read-only**: exit 0 clean,
exit 3 on any violation or un-audited surface.

- `db/src/db/graph_audit.py` — the whole-graph audit.
  - **TI-6 (§9.6)** — over the whole `resolution` table: same-subject pairs
    inside a declared mutually-exclusive predicate group (§13.4's four
    lifecycle tracks as four singleton groups — states within a track are
    mutually exclusive; states on different tracks co-hold by design,
    SIG-ONTO-061) violate when `valid_period`s overlap **and** `sys_period`s
    overlap. That independently re-verifies `resolution_no_overlap` (which
    guards only the live view) and extends it across all of belief time; the
    sanctioned close-then-supersede succession has disjoint `sys_period`s and
    stays legal by construction. Legal L1 claim-level contradiction is never
    flagged — the audit reads L3 resolutions only.
  - **TI-7 (§9.6)** — walks every declared supersedes/succession pointer
    surface (claim `revises_claim`/`retraction_of`; `entity_role`,
    `relationship`, `publication_disposition`, `human_eval_*`, and
    `evidence_artifact` supersession; the forward `superseded_by` links on
    `extraction`/`technology`/`vocab_predicate`; and the same-shaped lineage
    chains `entity.merged_into` + `evidence_capture.parent_capture_id`) —
    reporting every cycle (deduplicated by canonical rotation) and every
    pointer that runs off the graph (a dangling target is a termination
    failure, not a pass).
  - **Drift guard** — the surface registry is a *declaration*: the audit
    re-derives the live schema's self-referencing foreign keys from
    `pg_catalog` (all non-system namespaces) and fails the report on any
    self-FK the registry does not name, so a schema change cannot silently
    widen the supersedes surface.
- `db/src/db/cli.py` — `sig-db graph-audit --dsn …` (JSON report;
  exit 0/3).
- `db/README.md` — the audit command documented alongside the rebuild
  commands: what each leg proves, the exclusive-group declaration, and the
  CI leg's guarantee.
- `tests/db/test_whole_graph_audits.py` (+14, real PG18+PostGIS via
  testcontainers, reusing the P37.57a seeded-materialized-spine fixture) —
  the clean seeded spine audits 0 violations; injected TI-6 coexistence flags
  (a second live row via a deferred constraint **and** the belief-time case
  `resolution_no_overlap` cannot see); orthogonal lifecycle tracks and
  close-then-supersede belief succession stay legal; TI-7 chains terminate,
  2- and 3-cycles and off-graph targets flag exactly once; the self-FK drift
  guard fires on an undeclared surface; the CLI returns 0/3 correctly.
- `docs/build/COVERAGE_MATRIX.csv` — the three F2a-routed rows close:
  `SIG-ONTO-001` (six-layer model) and `SIG-STORE-004`/`SIG-STORE-005`
  (rebuildable projections / no sole home) → `covered+tested` / `MET`; the
  owed check named at R11 T4 (projection rebuild CI / layer-direction test /
  whole-graph audit) is delivered across P37.57a+b.

## Out of scope (named owners / prohibitions held)

- **Nightly scheduling of the audit** — the command and CI leg land here;
  wiring a scheduler is operator timing, not this row.
- **Live/staging posture** — no live legs, no production mutations, no DSN
  against a hosted spine; the audit is read-only by construction.
- No schema change — the audit reads the deployed schema; the drift guard
  exists precisely so future schema additions surface loudly.

## Honest notes

- The audit is *read-only*; it never writes to the spine. Violations it could
  only find on a spine that already carries them would be reported, never
  silently repaired — resolution stays a recorded decision.
- `physical_state` is declared in the exclusive-group set even where the
  deployed `vocab_predicate` does not yet register it — an unrealised group
  matches zero rows; the declaration is the complete §13.4 set, not the
  vocab diff.
